content.title: About
content.content: Soft‑serve frozen yogurt with a rich chocolate flavor is a low‑calorie dessert made from skim yogurt, sugar, and natural flavorings. When churned in a special machine it develops a light, creamy texture, and the addition of melted chocolate gives it a deep, indulgent taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yogurt‑based ice cream contains live probiotic cultures that support gut health.
The chocolate flavor is achieved with real cocoa mass, without artificial colorings.
Soft‑serve is served at about –12 °C, making it softer than traditional ice cream.
In many countries it is considered a healthier alternative to regular ice cream because of its lower fat content.
The soft‑serve technology was invented in the United States in the 1930s and has since spread worldwide.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Yogurt provides live bacterial cultures that can improve digestion and support the immune system.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with regular ice cream, yogurt‑based soft‑serve typically contains less saturated fat.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Yogurt is a good source of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Chocolate antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids, which may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yogurt supplies vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt‑based ice cream.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Some versions can contain a significant amount of added sugar, which should be considered in a balanced diet.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Storage temperature
items.content: Improper storage can cause the product to become grainy and lose its flavor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soft‑serve in cones, waffle cups, or bowls. Top with fresh berries, nuts, honey, or a sprinkle of grated chocolate for extra indulgence.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After opening, seal tightly to prevent absorption of other odors. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 30 minutes.

content.title: About
content.content: Ham croquette is a bite‑size fried snack made from minced ham, breadcrumbs, eggs and seasonings. It has a golden, crunchy crust and a tender, flavorful interior. The product is ready to eat after heating and works well as an appetizer, side dish or fast‑food component.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Croquettes originated in Europe in the 19th century as a way to use leftover meat.
The ham used is often smoked, giving the croquette its distinctive aroma.
Traditionally croquettes are hand‑shaped, but industrial production uses molding machines.
They are commonly served with sauces such as mustard, creamy or tomato‑based sauces.
In some countries ham croquettes are sold as a popular street‑food snack.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from meat supports oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, which help nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Croquettes deliver quick energy through a balance of protein, fat and carbohydrates.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune response and wound healing.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Ham is often salty, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Croquettes can contain notable amounts of saturated fat, which should be moderated.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergy or intolerance to pork.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Industrial croquettes may contain nitrites and other preservatives that some consumers avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat ham croquettes in an oven, microwave or skillet until the crust is golden. Serve hot with mustard, creamy or tomato sauce, and pair with vegetable sides.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep croquettes in the original packaging in the refrigerator at 0 °C to +4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C and reheat thoroughly before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: The unsalted mixed nuts with peanuts blend includes roasted almonds, cashews, hazelnuts, walnuts and peanuts. The nuts are not salted, preserving their natural flavor and aroma. This mix is suitable as a snack, in salads, baked goods and cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts, but are commonly included in nut mixes.
Nut mixes are popular in sports nutrition because of their high protein and healthy fat content.
Unsalted nuts retain more vitamins and minerals than their salted counterparts.
Varied nut sizes give the mix an interesting texture.
A well‑sealed package keeps the mix fresh for a long time.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The blend provides plant‑based protein important for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids support heart health and help lower bad cholesterol.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Nuts supply niacin, thiamine and folate, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals and antioxidants
items.content: Magnesium, phosphorus, zinc and vitamin E help strengthen bones and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber in the nuts promotes healthy gut function and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Nut and peanut allergy
items.content: People with allergies to nuts or peanuts may experience severe reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Nuts are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Whole nuts can pose a choking risk for young children; offer finely chopped pieces instead.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking nuts lowers its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Unsalted mixed nuts with peanuts are convenient as a standalone snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or used in sauces. For extra aroma, lightly toast the nuts in a dry pan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid.

content.title: About
content.content: The Balance Original Nutrition Bar is a balanced protein snack designed to support energy and recovery after workouts. It provides 20 g of protein, complex carbs, fiber, and a blend of vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bar is made from plant‑based pea and rice proteins, free from dairy.
It contains a mix of nuts, seeds, and dried fruit for natural sweetness without artificial sweeteners.
Each bar is packaged in a compostable wrapper that can be recycled at home.
Balance Original has been clinically tested for maintaining stable blood glucose after intense exercise.
The product is gluten‑free and soy‑lecithin‑free, suitable for those with sensitivities.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: 20 g of protein per serving helps muscle repair and keeps you feeling full.

items.title: Complex carbs and fiber
items.content: Oat flakes and inulin provide slow‑release energy and support digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B6 and B12 aid protein and carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Calcium, magnesium and iron contribute to bone health and oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The bar does not cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, making it suitable for athletes and those monitoring glucose levels.

items.title: Nut and seed allergy
items.content: The bar contains almonds, cashews and sunflower seeds, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: One bar contains about 250 kcal; consider total daily intake if you are watching calories.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although the sugar comes from natural fruit, people with diabetes should monitor consumption.

items.title: High fiber amount
items.content: Large amounts of fiber may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is convenient to take to the gym, work, or a hike. Eat it as a standalone snack or pair it with yogurt, fruit, or a protein shake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 30 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Ruffled plain potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes fried until crisp. They have a light salty taste and a characteristic wavy surface that holds dips and adds extra crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ruffled chips were introduced in the United States in the 1950s to increase surface area and improve dip retention.
A special corrugated cutter creates the wavy texture during slicing.
Starchy potatoes are chosen for their ability to become extra crunchy when fried.
In some countries they are colloquially called “potato waffles” because of their shape.
Plain ruffled chips are suitable for people who limit added flavors and salt.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Potato chips provide carbohydrates that quickly supply energy.

items.title: Potassium content
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C presence
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C survives rapid frying, offering antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: Unlike sweet snacks, plain ruffled chips contain virtually no sugar.

items.title: Easy digestibility
items.content: Thin slices cook quickly, making them easy to digest.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Chips are fried, so they are high in calories and fat.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Even plain chips often contain a modest amount of salt added during frying.

items.title: Aflatoxins
items.content: Improper storage of potatoes can lead to mold that produces aflatoxins.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes or to the frying oils used.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy chips as a snack on their own, with dips such as salsa, guacamole, or cheese sauce, or sprinkle them over salads for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from light. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent oil oxidation.
